data.cultural_impact: The name Philippa, derived from the Greek name Philippos, has a rich history and cultural significance. The name Philippa was quite popular in the Middle Ages, particularly among the nobility and ruling classes in Europe. It is also the name of several prominent figures throughout history, such as St. Philip the Deacon, a disciple of Jesus Christ, and Queen Philippa of England, who ruled during the late 13th and early 14th centuries.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Philippa holds spiritual significance as it comes from the Greek name Philippos, which means "horse-loving" or "horse-friendly." In Christian tradition, the name Philippa can be seen as a reminder of the symbolism of the horse in biblical literature. Horses are often depicted as powerful and majestic creatures, representing strength, endurance, and mobility, qualities that are sought after in those who follow God.

historical_references.context: Daughter of Guy of Flanders, Count of Hainault, and Jeanne of Navarre. She married Edward II of England in 1325. She was a strong and influential queen who helped to rule England during her husband's reign.
